stem: The nurse reviews the laboratory values used to estimate a client's calculated serum osmolality. Which group contains the three routine chemistry values used in the standard calculation, before accounting for ethanol when it is present?

options.C: Sodium, glucose, and blood urea nitrogen (BUN)

rationale: StatPearls describes calculated serum osmolality using sodium, blood urea nitrogen, and glucose, with ethanol included when it is present because ethanol is also osmotically active. Therefore C contains the three routine chemistry terms used in the calculation. The electrolyte trio in A, CBC values in B, and liver tests in D are not the core variables in this calculation.
educational_objective: Identify sodium, glucose, and BUN as the routine chemistry components of calculated serum osmolality while recognizing that ethanol must also be accounted for when present.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf — StatPearls
source_locator: Evaluation > osmolar-gap calculation: calculated serum osmolality incorporates sodium, BUN, glucose, and ethanol; ethanol should be accounted for because it is osmotically active
source_claim_supported: Sodium, glucose, and BUN are routine chemistry components used to calculate serum osmolality; ethanol is also incorporated when present.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Reduction of Risk Potential > Laboratory Values, printed p.43 / PDF p.47: compare client laboratory values to normal laboratory values; monitor client laboratory values
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Laboratory Values
correction_summary: Removed the colleague narrative and corrected the source item's implication that calculated osmolality universally consists of only three values. The stem now asks for the three routine chemistry terms while explicitly preserving the requirement to account for ethanol when present. Added exact source and blueprint locators and rebuilt concise parallel distractors.
audit_findings: C is the only option containing the standard sodium/glucose/BUN chemistry terms. The ethanol qualifier prevents an incomplete toxicology formula from being taught as universal. A, B, and D contain laboratory panels not used as the core terms in calculated osmolality. No arithmetic threshold, formula-unit ambiguity, second answer, or cueing remains.
